locality: Remnant of native vegetation near Wongan Hills, central wheat belt, Western Australia (see Fig. 1)
notes: No coordinates are printed in the source; the site is shown only as a point on the regional map in Fig. 1 (labelled 'Wongan Hills'), so latitude/longitude are left blank rather than estimated from the figure. Warmest/coolest month given as January/July respectively. This is the taxon's single known wild population, comprising 49 subpopulations (1-160 plants each) patchily distributed across the outcrop; the 9 subpopulations used for detailed study (sizes 2-163 plants) are not individually geocoded or given separate coordinates in the source, so are not broken out as separate location rows. Mean distance (+/-SE) from study subpopulations to the five nearest neighbouring subpopulations varied from 143+/-15 m to 320+/-49 m (not attributable to a single subpopulation pair, so not retained as a numeric column here).
